title: Longest Run of Ones

concept.title: Tracking a current run
body: To find the longest run of equal values, keep two numbers: the length of the **current run** and the **best** length seen so far. A one extends the current run, a zero resets it to zero. After every step update the best.

body.code:
cur = best = 0
for x in a:
    cur = cur + 1 if x == 1 else 0
    best = max(best, cur)

body: The same "current and best" pair works for longest streaks of anything: equal letters, increasing numbers, days in a row.

statement: You are given an array that contains only 0 and 1. Print the length of the longest block of consecutive 1s.
inputFormat: The second line has `n` numbers, each 0 or 1.
outputFormat: Print one integer: the longest run of ones (0 if there is no 1).

examples.note: The longest block is the three ones in the middle.

hints: Remember how long the run is that you are in right now.
On a 1 add one to the current run; on a 0 set it to zero.
After each element, keep the larger of the best and the current run.

starter.python:
n = int(input())
a = list(map(int, input().split()))
